In this episode, Gary Zukav takes on a question that may seem minor on the surface but opens into something much deeper: does casual alcohol use block the creation of authentic power? Rather than offering a simple yes or no, Gary reframes the question entirely, inviting listeners to examine not what they are doing, but why. He challenges the idea of “casual” behavior altogether, calling instead for conscious, intentional living rooted in an awareness of one’s creative power.

At the heart of Gary’s response is the question of intention. Whether it is a drink at dinner, a smile across a room, or any habitual behavior, the real question is always the same: is this action coming from love or from fear? 

Gary illustrates how what appears to be harmless social drinking can, upon closer examination, be a way of masking discomfort, seeking approval, or attempting to manipulate how others perceive you – all expressions of a frightened part of the personality.

The way forward is not judgment, but awareness. When life energy is used consciously and intentionally, with a genuine desire to contribute, connect, and create from love, even the smallest choices become opportunities to create authentic power.

What You’ll Discover in This Episode:

(00:43) — Gary responds to the question of casual alcohol use by widening the lens: rather than evaluating the behavior itself, he invites listeners to examine how they are using their life energy – and whether they are doing so consciously and intentionally.

(01:30) — Gary asks the essential question behind any behavior: what is your intention? Is drinking – or any social habit – an attempt to mask feelings of fear, loosen up for approval, or influence how others feel about you? If so, that intention originates in fear, not in love.

(02:32) — Gary offers examples of what it looks like to redirect life energy toward love: contributing to others, moving toward meaning and purpose, and choosing harmony, cooperation, and reverence for life over the need to please.

(03:00) — Gary shares that people in his programs have discovered their “casual” alcohol use was far less casual than they believed – and that the difficulty of giving it up revealed something important about the frightened parts of their personality that were active.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your notebook and think of a habit in your life that you have labeled “casual” or “harmless.” It doesn’t have to be alcohol – it could be anything you reach for when you feel uncomfortable, anxious, or unseen. Ask yourself honestly: what is my intention in this moment? Am I acting from love – from a genuine desire to contribute, connect, or create – or am I acting from fear? Write down what you notice, without judgment.

In this DeepCast, Gary Zukav continues his exploration of temptation, picking up where Part 1 left off, and going deeper into what it truly means to choose between love and fear. Drawing on his own experience with addiction, Gary reveals that temptation is never a matter of right or wrong, good or bad. It is always, at its core, a choice about what experiences you intend to bring into your life and a recognition that no one else can make that choice for you.

Building on that foundation, Gary introduces two dimensions that Part 1 only touched on: the danger of attachment (even to “good” choices) and the profound journey of uncovering every part of your personality, including the darkest ones. Through the story of a Tibetan monk who nearly lost his compassion for his Chinese torturers, 

Gary illustrates the staggering range of emotional capability within every human being, and the courage it takes to meet all of it without judgment.

The way through all of it, Gary reveals, is the creation of authentic power – not through willpower or moral superiority, but through the patient, courageous practice of emotional awareness, responsible choice, and compassion for others and for yourself.

What You’ll Discover in This Episode:

(00:43) — Gary revisits the new consciousness framework for temptation: the choice is never between good and bad, but between the experiences you are choosing to create for yourself—and only you can make that choice.

(01:26) — Gary shares his own experience with addiction and the terrifying moment of standing at an equal crossroads.

(04:17) — Gary warns against the trap of attachment to “right” choices: congratulating yourself for choosing well can become a subtle expression of fear, superiority, and separation which is a choice for fear, not love.

(06:10) — Gary traces the long arc of creating authentic power, sharing his early experience of challenging his anger — from clenching his fists in front of someone who enraged him, to gradually relaxing, to eventually experiencing compassion – showing that this is a process, not a single moment.

(08:08) — Gary opens up the full, confronting range of the human psyche: from Christ-like love to the desire to destroy, all of it lives within you. Repulsion at any part of yourself is judgment – and judgment is attachment, which is the cause of suffering.

(12:39) — Gary shares the story of the Tibetan monk who told the Dalai Lama he had been in danger of losing his compassion for his Chinese torturers as the clearest illustration of what it looks like to hold the full range of human experience with compassion.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your notebook and think of a part of yourself that you find difficult to accept such as a reaction, an impulse, a feeling you’d rather not admit is there. Without judgment, ask yourself: am I repulsed by this because I am judging it? And if I am judging it, what does that tell me about my attachment to it? Sit with that honestly. Then ask: is there someone in my life right now whose behavior I find hard to stomach? Write down what bothers you most about them – and then, quietly, look for those same things in yourself. Notice what happens in your body when you do. That softening – however small – is the beginning of compassion.

In this Soul Snack, Gary Zukav responds to a deeply personal question from a listener who has spent a lifetime feeling unseen and judged – a tall, big‑boned woman born with leg deformities who believes her physical experience may be karmic but does not know what for.

Gary reframes the question by drawing a distinction between the personality – the earth suit the soul wears during its time in the Earth school – and the soul itself, which is powerful, compassionate, and without limit. When you focus only on the appearance of the earth suit, he suggests, you miss the vastness of who you are.

The most profound insight Gary offers is that her experience may not be a karmic burden at all, but a karmic gift – one that has uniquely positioned her to see others as souls rather than surfaces.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:02) — Gary opens with a reflection on the transformation of human consciousness and the choice in each moment between living in gratitude and awe or in fear and despair.

(01:35) — A listener shares her lifelong experience of judgment and invisibility, asking Gary whether her appearance is karmic and what it means.

(03:51) — Gary introduces the distinction between soul and personality: the personality is an earth suit chosen for a specific journey, while the soul is a powerful, creative, compassionate presence.

(05:30) — Gary reframes karma not as punishment but as an exquisite gift – her experiences have prepared her to see others as souls rather than appearances, with uncommon generosity and without judgment.

(07:19) — Gary closes by reminding us that no aspect of a personality appears by accident. The soul chooses its earth suit to create the experiences it needs in order to evolve.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Think of someone – or perhaps yourself – whom you have viewed through the lens of appearance rather than soul. Ask yourself: What did I miss by seeing only the surface? Sit with that question today, and consider what it would mean to move through the world seeing every person, including yourself, as a soul first.

In this DeepCast, Gary Zukav reveals what he considers the single most fundamental element of spiritual growth and self‑transformation – temptation. Far from the Western view of temptation as an external evil force, Gary reframes it as a gracious dynamic in the universe – a purposeful invitation to choose between love and fear. Drawing on the lives of the Buddha and Jesus, he shows that every human being meets the same essential crossroads that the great spiritual masters met.

Gary challenges the idea that temptation originates outside of us. He reveals it instead as the activity of the frightened parts of the personality – a kind of dress rehearsal for a negative karmic event that places the full power of choice in your hands.

The answer lies in the twin pillars of authentic power: emotional awareness and responsible choice. When you recognize the physical sensations and thoughts of a frightened part of your personality, temptation shifts from a trap into a teacher.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

(01:04) — Gary names the core dynamic – temptation – and contrasts the Western, externalized view with the perspective of the new consciousness, in which temptation does not originate outside of you, but within the frightened parts of your personality.

(05:52) — Gary draws on the lives of the Buddha and Jesus to show that the great spiritual masters met the same temptations that you meet – with nothing to guide them toward one choice or another except their own awareness.

(11:59) — Gary introduces temptation as a dress rehearsal for a negative karmic event – the moment just before choice becomes action and energy becomes matter. When you act on temptation, you create karma. When you choose otherwise, the soul moves freely.

(17:44) — Gary outlines the two pillars of authentic power – emotional awareness and responsible choice – and explains that recognizing the sensations and thoughts of a frightened part of your personality is the first step toward choosing differently.

(23:37) — Gary closes Part 1 with a reminder that moment by moment, life brings you to a choice between love and fear. The choice is not what you intend. The choice is the action you take.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your notebook and think of a moment when you felt the pull of a temptation. Ask yourself: what frightened part of my personality was at work? What did it feel like in your body – in your chest, your throat, your solar plexus? Then ask the deeper question: were you choosing from love or from fear? Write down what you notice, without judgment. Temptation is not your enemy – it is the universe’s gracious invitation to know yourself more fully and choose, consciously, who you truly are.

In this Soul Snack, Gary Zukav explores one of the most common – and most misunderstood – responses to guilt: the apology. He challenges the assumption that saying “I’m sorry” is inherently loving or helpful, and he reveals that most apologies do not arise from love, but from fear.

Using simple, vivid examples – from apologizing for a late reply to his team, to choosing to celebrate a young man’s father rather than offering condolences – 

Gary shows how apologies often function as unconscious attempts to gain approval, avoid conflict, or manage how others feel about us. 

Beneath the surface, they reflect a frightened part of the personality reaching outward for relief instead of turning inward toward growth.

The most loving response to guilt is not an apology. It is the conscious choice to challenge the frightened part of the personality that guilt activates, and to cultivate authentic power instead.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

  • (00:00) — Gary opens the exploration of apologies by asking when – if ever – saying “I’m sorry” is truly appropriate, viewed through the lens of authentic power.
  • (01:26) — After apologizing to his team for a late reply, a spiritual partner asks Gary whether that apology came from a frightened part of his personality – one wanting to remain liked rather than acting with genuine intention.
  • (02:51) — Instead of offering condolences to a young man whose father had passed, Gary chose to celebrate the father’s life – showing how reflexive apologies often arise from habit rather than conscious love.
  • (03:51) — Emotional pain does not originate with other people. It arises from interior dynamics – frightened parts of the personality activated by others’ words, not caused by them.
  • (05:49) — Apologizing for someone else’s emotional pain means taking responsibility for an interior dynamic that belongs entirely to them – one only they have the power to transform.
  • (06:48) — Gary reframes the core choice in every difficult interaction: react from fear, or respond with love. That choice is always ours.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Think of a recent moment when you felt the impulse to apologize – to a colleague, a loved one, or even a stranger. Ask yourself: Was that apology coming from love, or from fear? Was it an attempt to genuinely connect, or to manage how someone else felt about you? Sit with that question today, and notice what it reveals about the parts of your personality that were active in that moment.

In this DeepCast, Gary Zukav shares one of the most astonishing realizations of his spiritual journey: that the words he wrote nearly fifty years ago – in his award‑winning book The Dancing Wu Li Masters – described with perfect precision the truth he has since lived, learned, and embodied through decades of experience, love, loss, and guidance from his angelic teacher, Genesis. Drawing on the language of quantum physics, 

Gary returns to the physicists’ most profound and paradigm‑shattering conclusion: that what exists is one unbroken wholeness, no aspect of which is separate from any other – and that this is not a theory. It is what you are.

At the heart of this Soul Feast is a question Gary brought to Genesis in frustration and wonder: Why? Why did I have to go through all of that? The decades of searching, suffering, loving, growing, expanding – all of it. And Genesis answered with four words that dissolved every remaining illusion of intellectual accomplishment: So you won’t know it. Not know it as information. Know it as experience. Know it as life itself.

The miracle, Gary reveals, is not something that happens to you. It is what you are. You are the universe – and the universe is love. That is the only reason to do anything at all.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

  • (00:44) — Gary begins with the story of writing The Dancing Wu Li Masters at 35, drawn by a felt sense that quantum mechanics revealed the precise edge where the intellect ends – and where what lies beyond it begins.
  • (05:22) — Gary returns to the breathtaking conclusion he wrote half a century ago: that reality may be one unbroken wholeness, no aspect of which is separate from any other – and shares the shock of recognizing those words as an exact description of what he knows now.
  • (10:00) — Gary reflects on the path that brought him to this moment: Genesis, Linda, the love he never imagined was possible, and the understanding that every experience – however difficult – was created to meet and transform the frightened parts of his personality.
  • (14:18) — Genesis answers Gary’s deepest “why” with four words: So you won’t know it. Gary explores what it means to carry wisdom not as information, but as lived experience.
  • (17:36) — Gary traces the arc of human evolution – from five‑sensory to multi‑sensory to universal human – and explains that authentic power, the alignment of personality with soul, is the path itself, and that love is what awaits on the other side of every choice.
  • (22:43) — Gary arrives at the word that holds all of it: miracle. Not something outside of you – but what you are. You are the universe expressing itself uniquely in every moment, through every choice rooted in love or fear.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your notebook and sit with what Gary shares in this DeepCast. Think of a moment in your life – something painful, confusing, or hard to understand – and ask yourself: What if this experience wasn’t something that happened to me, but something that happened for me, so that I would know it, not as a concept, but as lived truth? Sit with that. Then ask: in the choices I made today, was I creating from love – from harmony, compassion, and kindness – or from fear? Write down what you notice, without judgment. The miracle isn’t waiting somewhere ahead of you. It is you, here, now, choosing.

In this episode, Gary Zukav answers a listener’s question that many have quietly wondered about: what determines a soulmate? His answer is expansive – every person on this planet, all seven billion incarnate souls, is in truth a soulmate. The more meaningful question is not who your soulmate is, but how you choose to relate to the souls whose paths cross your own.

Gary introduces spiritual partnership as the most conscious and fulfilling way to relate to another soul – a relationship between equals, co‑created with intention for the purpose of spiritual growth, in which each partner chooses how they show up for one another.

The hallmark of a true soulmate connection: partners stay together as long as they grow together spiritually – and share with one another what they fear most could destroy the partnership.

What You’ll Discover in This Episode:

(00:43) — Gary offers a new way to understand the word soulmate: with seven billion incarnate souls on this planet, every person whose path crosses yours is, in truth, your soulmate.

(01:33) — The deeper question is not who your soulmate is, but how you choose to relate – with awareness, love, and spiritual intention toward a fellow soul on a shared journey.

(02:32) — Gary describes spiritual partnership as a conscious relationship between equals created for spiritual growth, in which partners stay together as long as both grow – and share what they fear most could damage the relationship. He reflects on his 26‑year partnership with Linda Francis as an example.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Reflect on a key relationship in your life – a partner, friend, or colleague. Ask yourself: Am I relating to this person as a fellow soul, or through the lens of fear and habit? What would it look like to bring more consciousness and spiritual intention into this connection? Pause with that question today, and notice what arises.

In this DeepCast, Gary Zukav turns the lens inward with one of the most fundamental questions a human being can ask: What are you? Drawing from the perspective of the new consciousness:

Gary invites listeners beyond the limitations of the intellect and five-sensory perception, inviting them to see themselves not as personalities born on a date and destined to die – but as immortal souls and unique expressions of a universe made entirely of love.

At the heart of this Soul Feast is a distinction that changes everything: the difference between the “little you” – the personality, the name you carry, the self that will one day leave the Earth School – and the “big You,” the soul that is eternal, exists in non-physical reality, and is always home. The new consciousness now makes it possible to experience both at the same time. Yet most of us remain anchored in the old consciousness, where identity stopped at the edges of the physical body and power meant manipulation and control.

Gary offers a profound reorientation: you are your perceptions, a unique expression of the Universe, and above all, you are love – and every choice you make, in love or in fear, shapes what that unique expression becomes.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

(02:49) — Gary introduces the distinction between the “little you” (personality) and the “big You” (soul) –  two aspects of the self that the new consciousness now makes it possible to experience at the same time – and why this changes everything about identity, power, and what it means to be alive in the Earth School.

(05:48) — Gary reframes the difference between love and fear not as morality or ethics, but as an energetic difference in who you are – and explains how aligning personality with soul is the new consciousness definition of authentic power.

(08:56) — Gary shares the teaching that transformed his own experience: you are your perceptions. This insight opens the door to experiencing the universe not as something outside of you, but as something you are.

(11:51) — Drawing on the words of Jesus – “the kingdom of heaven is within you” – Gary illuminates what it means to be a unique expression of the universe, and why the intellect alone was never designed to take us there.

(17:59) — Free will is the power to choose love or fear in every moment. Choices rooted in fear create painful, contracting consequences; choices rooted in love create healthy, expansive, creative experiences – and together, those choices become your unique expression of the universe.

(24:11) — Gary closes with an invitation to experiment with choosing love – not romantic or sentimental love, but the love that is what you are – and shares his practice of following deep meaning as a compass for authentic living.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your notebook and sit with the question Gary poses in this DeepCast: What are you? Begin with the words, “I am my perceptions.” Sit with that for a few moments. Notice what you see, what you hear, what you feel – and notice that there is no separate “you” standing apart from those perceptions. Then ask yourself: in the choices I made today, was I acting from the big You – love, harmony, reverence for life – or reacting from the little you, from fear? Write down what you notice, without judgment. That honest awareness is where the creation of Authentic Power begins.

Blog Title: Soul Snack #85: The Mirror of Compassion: Why How You Treat Others Reflects How You Treat Yourself
Short Description: Create the life you desire by choosing love over fear.

In this Soul Snack, Gary Zukav and Linda Francis explore the profound connection between compassion for yourself and compassion for others. 

Gary reveals that the creation of Authentic Power and the cultivation of compassion are, in truth, the same path. 

Every tool of the new consciousness – from multisensory perception to emotional awareness and responsible choice – serves as a direct gateway to the practice of compassion.

Gary explains that the frightened parts of the personality are the parts that lack compassion. The very same part of you that judges or feels impatience toward another person is inevitably directing those same judgements, impatience, and anger inward. Linda deepens this insight: when we choose to judge another, we create that same experience in our own self and in our own bodies, making compassion for the self and others impossible in that moment.

Gary also introduces the dynamic of projection – the tendency of the personality to see in others what the frightened parts refuse to acknowledge within ourselves. By recognizing these projections, we can identify the internal “curriculum” that needs healing.

True compassion becomes available the moment you step out of the control of a frightened part of your personality and into the domain of Love. That movement, repeated with intention, is the fundamental mechanism through which Authentic Power is created.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:53) — Gary explains why creating authentic power and creating compassion are one and the same practice – and why everything already learned in the Earth School applies directly, with no need to start over.

(01:30) — The frightened parts of the personality are the parts with no compassion: the same parts judging, criticizing, or feeling impatient with others are doing the exact same thing inward.

(03:28) — Linda illuminates how judging someone else simultaneously creates that experience in your own body – and why compassion for yourself and others cannot exist at the same time as judgment.

(03:47) — Gary clarifies the powerful two-way connection: you cannot have compassion for someone else without having compassion for yourself – and you cannot have compassion for yourself without having it for others. Both exist in the domain of love.

(04:16) — Gary introduces the practice of projection: writing down everything a frightened part of your personality dislikes in another person – in detail – and then looking for those same qualities honestly within yourself.

(05:26) — Why understanding compassion in the mind is not enough: Linda and Gary discuss the essential role of emotional awareness in actually feeling what you are challenging, so that frightened parts of the personality begin to lose their control.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take a moment to bring to mind someone you have been judging, criticizing, or feeling impatient with. Write down everything about them that a frightened part of your personality doesn’t like – in detail. Then, with courage and openness, look for those same qualities within yourself. This is the practice of projection awareness, and one of the most direct doorways into compassion for yourself and others. Ask yourself: What would it feel like to meet this moment with love instead of judgment? Pause with that question today, and notice what arises.

Drawing on the perspective of the new consciousness, he reframes parenthood and every interaction with a child as a sacred opportunity to practice conscious, soul-centered love.

At the heart of this Soul Feast lies a powerful distinction: 

When we see children only through the lens of their physical bodies and undeveloped minds, we miss the reality of who they truly are. 

Children do not simply emerge from the womb – they arrive from eternity, carrying the full creative power and accumulated experience of souls that have incarnated many times before. Recognizing that your child is an ancient soul changes everything about the way you relate to them.

The intention behind each moment – Love or Fear – shapes not only the child’s experience but the parent’s own spiritual evolution. In this Soul Snack, Gary Zukav and Linda Francis explore the concept of freestyling as a powerful metaphor for living authentically. Drawing from the world of sports – skiing, snowboarding, and gymnastics – Gary illuminates how the greatest athletes broke free from rigid conventions to create entirely new categories of movement. That same liberation, he teaches, is available to every person willing to move beyond the narrow expectations set by the frightened parts of their personality.

Gary explains that the frightened parts of the personality are what define the parameters – the narrow band of what feels “acceptable” in life. Whether in writing, relationships, or personal ambition, those fear-based limitations keep people performing the same routines. But when a person chooses to act from a loving part of their personality instead, they step into a domain that is entirely new, created by you, by choosing love.

Creating authentic power is the ultimate freestyle. 

It is the practice of not being controlled by fear in the pursuit of external power and instead following the call of the heart and soul – even when that direction is subtle, uncertain, or not yet fully understood.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

  • (00:00) — How elite athletes in freestyle sports broke the rules of their disciplines and why that same courage applies to the creation of Authentic Power in the Earth School.
  • (01:34) — Why the frightened parts of the personality set the parameters – and what happens when you make the Responsible Choice to act from a loving part of your personality instead.
  • (02:11) — Gary shares how his own writing process changed when he released the pursuit of external power (writing what he thought “should” be written) and instead followed where the energy of his Soul’s intention led.
  • (03:00) — The difference between the pursuit of external power (money, status, sex) and the creation of Authentic Power – following what your heart is genuinely calling you toward.
  • (03:25) — Gary’s personal story of recognizing the frequency of Linda Francis the moment she arrived, and how that subtle but undeniable signal from the Soul led to thirty years of Spiritual Partnership.
  • (04:33) — A reflection on Visual 31: which of the five figures represents your personality today – and which one represented you yesterday as you navigate the Earth School?

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take a moment to reflect on the areas of your life where the frightened parts of your personality have been setting the parameters. Where have you been staying inside the narrow band of what feels “acceptable” – in your relationships, your work, your creativity, or your goals? Ask yourself: What would I do if I were freestyling? What direction is your heart calling you toward that you have been hesitant to follow? Pause with that question today, and notice what arises.

In this deeply moving continuation, Gary Zukav and Scarlett Lewis – founder of the Choose Love Movement – explore the interior landscape of Authentic Power: what it truly means to choose love not just as a feeling, but as a conscious act of will in the face of grief, fear, and loss. Together, they trace the path from forgiveness to compassion, and from compassion to personal transformation.

At the center of their exchange is a truth both hard-won and universal: that the frightened parts of our personalities – anger, judgment, resentment, and righteousness – are not enemies to defeat but opportunities for deeper awareness. Scarlett shares how forgiving the individual responsible for the death of her son, Jesse, was not an act of denial, but of liberation – and how that conscious choice led her to feel genuine compassion, and ultimately, love.

In today’s episode, Gary Zukav reflects on a pivotal moment in his life—meeting Oprah Winfrey and the profound impact that experience had on his journey. 

He shares how this encounter brought him from the quiet solitude of Mount Shasta, a small and serene mountain community in Northern California where he spent much of his time engaging in outdoor activities, into the national spotlight, forever changing his life. 

This unexpected meeting not only brought his work to millions but also ignited a transformation in Gary’s life, challenging him to navigate the complexities of fame and recognition while staying true to his spiritual path.

Gary expresses his deep gratitude for the lessons he learned from Oprah, a woman of great integrity, and the importance of following a life of true meaning and purpose. 

Gary also introduces his powerful sailing ship metaphor, offering a thoughtful explanation of the intricate relationship between our personality and soul.

Through this metaphor, he illustrates how we can steer our lives, making conscious choices about which ‘crew members’—our emotions, thoughts, and behaviors—we allow to guide us through life’s challenges. 

This concept serves as a profound reminder of the importance of aligning our actions with our soul’s true purpose, rather than being driven by fear, ego, or societal expectations.

As you listen, you’ll gain insights into:

► How authentic connections can lead to transformative experiences

► Why fame and recognition aren’t the true path to fulfillment

► The real essence of empowerment

What Gary Discusses in This Episode:

In this DeepCast Soul Feast, Gary Zukav examines a phrase so familiar it has become almost meaningless: “we’re all in this together.” Rather than treating it as a feel-good sentiment, Gary explores what it actually means through the lens of the new consciousness now emerging in humanity, revealing that this togetherness is not emotional reassurance but a literal description of how reality works in the Earth School.

He explains that in the old consciousness, power meant manipulation and control, built on a hard line between “in here” and “out there.” The new consciousness dissolves that line, showing that what happens within us creates effects beyond the reach of the intellect. This raises the deeper question Gary poses: if every person we encounter is a soul, not just a personality, how are we meant to relate to one another?

The answer lies in shifting from relating personality-to-personality to relating soul-to-soul.

Replacing judgment and reaction with reverence for the essence beneath every person’s appearance and behavior.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast

(00:02) — Why a Deepcast is different from a podcast: it doesn’t change you – your resonance with what you hear reveals something already within you.

(03:06) — How recognizing a frightened or loving part of your personality in someone else is the first step in creating Authentic Power.

(08:59) — Old‑consciousness power was manipulation and control rooted in separation; new consciousness dissolves the line between “in here” and “out there,” redefining what power even means.

(12:07) — The people in your life are never accidental – they are souls you have encountered before, and the new consciousness invites you to revere rather than dismiss them.

(14:58) — Even the most heinous personalities in history are souls incarnate, which reframes the real question from “how do I deal with others” to “how do I relate soul to soul?”

(19:56) — Gary previews the next topic, attachment, and closes with a Soul Step inviting listeners to track what resonates with them throughout the week.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

This week, notice the people who cross your path – the ones you’re drawn to and the ones you’d rather avoid. Pause before you judge their appearance or behavior, and ask yourself: what might I see if I looked past the shell to the soul beneath? Write down what comes up, whether you agree with it or resist it. You are not here to force yourself into reverence – you are here to notice where you already are, and where there is still learning.

In this Soul Snack, Linda Francis addresses a question many people quietly carry: what do you do when you don’t like what’s happening in your life? Rather than offering a strategy to fix outer circumstances, Linda redirects attention inward – to the part of the personality that is reacting to the discomfort in the first place.

That reaction, she explains, often comes from a frightened part of the personality.

When fear is present, it becomes difficult to see what else is possible, both in the situation and in oneself.

The real work begins with noticing – feeling what is happening in the body, becoming aware of physical sensations, and recognizing fear as it arises.

The solution Linda offers is simple but not easy: once fear is recognized in the body, a different choice becomes available – one that does not go along with the fear’s narrative that everything is going wrong.

In this DeepCast episode, Gary Zukav explores one of the most commonly accepted ideas in modern self‑help culture – that setting boundaries is essential to healthy living. From the perspective of the old and new consciousness:

Gary reframes the entire notion of boundaries, showing that what once supported human survival is no longer aligned with where human evolution is now moving.

The old consciousness rests on a fundamental separation between “in here” and “out there,” and boundaries naturally arise from that divide. As the new consciousness emerges, that perceived wall between self and other begins to dissolve. The very premise that there is an “other” to protect yourself from is revealed as an illusion created by a frightened part of your personality.

Gary offers a clarifying question that goes directly to the heart of the matter: each time you feel the impulse to set a boundary, ask whether you are protecting a frightened part of your personality – or a loving one. A loving part of your personality needs no protection.

What You’ll Discover in This Episode:

(00:00) — The unprecedented transformation of human consciousness now underway – and the choice it places before every person: gratitude or fear, love or despair.

(02:37) — Why old‑consciousness power – manipulation and control – is no longer enough, and what authentic power actually means: aligning your personality with your soul.

(08:31) — The old consciousness draws an uncrossable line between in here and out there. The new consciousness dissolves it – and with it, the very foundation on which boundaries are built.

(11:39) — The concept of “the other” is a product of fear and imagination. Following fear leads only to emptiness; following love leads to meaning, purpose, and connection.

(15:03) — Authentic power is built by finding every frightened part of your personality, experiencing each one intimately, and choosing to move beyond it.

(22:00) — The question Gary leaves with every listener: when you set a boundary, who are you really protecting – a frightened part of your personality, or a loving one?

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

The next time you feel the impulse to set a boundary, pause before you act. Ask yourself honestly: what am I protecting right now? Is it a frightened part of your personality speaking, or a loving one? Sit with whatever comes up without judgment. You are not here to condemn yourself for your fear – you are here to see it clearly, and then to choose. That is how spiritual growth happens: one conscious choice at a time.

In this DeepCast episode, Gary Zukav reveals one of Earth School’s most profound truths: the world around you is not a backdrop to your life – it is a mirror. Every reaction, judgment, and moment of dislike or admiration you experience in others is a direct reflection of something alive within yourself. Drawing on Carl Jung’s concept of projection:

Gary brings clarity to how the qualities that trigger the strongest responses in us are the very qualities we have yet to fully recognize in ourselves.

Gary challenges the habit of looking outside yourself for the source of your feelings. Whether it is a person whose generosity moves you or someone whose behavior repulses you, the old consciousness looks outward for explanation. The new consciousness turns inward – using those same reactions as precise guidance about what is activating a frightened part or a loving part of your personality.

The path to self-knowledge is not found through introspection alone – it is revealed in every encounter, every irritation, and every moment of unexpected beauty the world places in front of you.

What You’ll Discover in This Episode:

(00:02) — A shift in human consciousness is underway – and the choice between gratitude and fear is one you are making moment by moment.

(02:59) — Carl Jung’s concept of projection: when a quality feels too painful to acknowledge in yourself, you see it in the people around you instead – and you resist what you see.

(06:23) — The world is not teaching you about others. It is teaching you about yourself – everything you need to know to create meaning and joy in your life.

(09:14) — Every reaction to someone else is a projection. Place your attention inside – in your chest, your throat, your solar plexus – and discover whether a frightened part or a loving part of your personality is speaking.

(12:12) — The takes‑one‑to‑know‑one principle works both ways: the grace and saintliness you admire in others are already active within you.

(19:03) — You are not separate from the world you observe. Every choice you make ripples outward through the fabric of existence.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

The next time someone triggers a strong reaction in you – admiration or irritation – write down everything you notice about that person. That evening, look for each quality in yourself. Do not rush past anything. The things that feel most impossible to own are often the ones most worth finding. You are not here to judge yourself – you are here to know yourself. That is the gift the world is always offering.

In this Soul Snack, Linda Francis shares a story she has never forgotten – one that reshaped the way she moves through the world. Separated from Gary at a retreat and seated among a group of unfamiliar Texas attorneys, Linda felt a frightened part of her personality become active immediately. The pull to withdraw was strong, and yet she chose to stay present with her experience, and in that moment, to create Authentic Power.

The familiar often disguises itself as preference and comfort, but beneath it is the quiet refusal of the soul’s growth.

Linda’s experience reveals how much we lose when we move only toward what feels safe and known. The transformation, she discovered, is not willpower but curiosity – a choice to stop judging and start opening.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:00) — Gary opens with a reflection on the transformation of human consciousness and the choice each of us faces: to live in gratitude and awe, or to follow the pull of fear and despair.

(00:43) — Linda shares the story: arriving late to a retreat, separated from Gary, and seated among men she immediately began to judge.

(01:35) — Linda describes the frightened parts of her personality that became active – the pull toward comfort – and how she chose to move through her experience rather than away from it.

(02:10) — Linda reflects on the shift that followed when she stopped pushing the men away and opened to what she could learn from them.

(02:45) — Linda shares the broader principle: limiting ourselves to the familiar is a pattern of the frightened personality, and experimenting with discomfort becomes a powerful way to create Authentic Power.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Think of a moment when you avoided something unfamiliar because it felt uncomfortable. Ask yourself: What frightened parts were driving that choice? What might I have missed? Sit with that today – and consider what one small step toward the unfamiliar might look like right now.

In this Soul Feast, Gary Zukav brings the Temptation series to its most expansive conclusion – revealing that the greatest temptation you will ever face is not a single dramatic moment of crisis, but the one unfolding right now, in this moment, and in every moment of your life. Drawing on his own experience of writing The Dancing Wu Li Masters against impossible odds,

Gary illuminates the difference between what a frightened part of the personality creates and what a loving part of the personality sees – and why that distinction is everything.

Gary challenges the familiar notion that temptation is something you wait for or recognize only in rare, high‑stakes moments. Instead, he reframes it as the constant, ever‑present invitation of Earth School itself – the ongoing choice between love and fear that lives in every reaction, every judgment, every hope you allow or dismiss. The frightened parts of your personality do not announce themselves. They feel righteous, satisfying, and completely justified in the moment.

The path through temptation is not avoidance – it is awareness. When you learn to recognize the physical sensations and emotional charge of a frightened part of your personality, you gain the power to consciously redirect your attention toward a loving part and choose from there instead.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

(01:42) — You are not only a body and a mind. You are a soul – immortal, multi‑incarnational, and in Earth School for one essential reason: to learn to choose love instead of fear.

(04:56) — Temptation is not a rough draft. It is the final dress rehearsal of a frightened part of your personality – every line memorized, every move set – presenting itself one last time before the action that creates karma.

(09:15) — The greatest temptation is not a dramatic moment you will recognize when it arrives. It is the way you hold the possibilities in front of you right now – as reachable or out of reach. That act of seeing, or refusing to see, shapes probability itself.

(13:54) — Eighteen months of rejection letters, mounting debt, and no credentials – and Gary never doubted The Dancing Wu Li Masters would be published. Not because he willed it. Because he simply saw it. That is a loving part of the personality at full strength.

(20:59) — This temptation does not end. It lasts as long as you are in Earth School, because having a personality means having both loving and frightened parts. That is not a flaw in the design. That is the design.

(24:21) — For 350,000 years, humans believed power meant control. The new consciousness changes that – you are not at the mercy of the world; you are its co‑creator. There is no “in here” and “out there.” There is only you, choosing, moment by moment, what you become.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out a small notebook – something you can keep close throughout your day. Each time you notice a strong reaction, a dismissal, a craving, or a judgment, write it down. Ask yourself: was that coming from a frightened part of my personality or a loving one? How did it feel in your body – in your chest, your gut, the tension in your jaw? At the end of the day, look back at what you wrote. You are not looking for perfection. You are looking for awareness. That awareness is the gracious gift of temptation – divinity’s direct message, straight to your heart.

Every power struggle, Gary explains, is rooted in the pursuit of external power – the drive to change, manage, or dominate what exists outside of us.

Whether we are clashing with a partner or a roommate, or reaching for a fresh start in a new city, the horizontal path keeps us moving sideways. In the Earth School, we often find that nothing truly changes because we haven’t changed the frightened parts of our personality that are driving the conflict.

The vertical path is different. It is the path of spiritual evolution. It invites us to turn inward – to practice Emotional Awareness – and in doing so, to begin aligning our personality with our Soul. This alignment allows us to access the kind of Authentic Power that Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. brought to bear on the world – a power rooted in love, not in the control of others.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

  • (00:43) — The Internal Dynamics of a Power Struggle: Gary defines the core of every power struggle – the pursuit of external power through the impulse to control – and reveals how it operates at every scale, from intimate partnerships to international conflict.
  • (01:26) — The Horizontal Path and its Limitations: Attempting to find relief by changing partners, circumstances, or cities defines the horizontal path. Without internal change, the same frightened parts of the personality follow us wherever we go in the Earth School.
  • (01:56) — The Vertical Path: Gary introduces the only path that creates real transformation – the vertical path of spiritual evolution – and connects it to the emergence of Authentic Power.
  • (02:14) — The Fragility of External Power: For millennia, our species has sought safety through external power – competition, hoarding, and exploitation. Gary explains why this foundation now threatens our survival and the evolution of our consciousness.
  • (02:54) — The Soul’s Intentions: Harmony, cooperation, sharing, and a reverence for Life are the Soul’s true intentions. Gary describes the creative tension humanity now inhabits as these values begin to emerge from the new consciousness.
  • (03:27) — Authentic Power in Action: As we align our personality with our Soul, we begin to cultivate the kind of power that moves mountains – the Authentic Power of Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr., anchored in a life lived from the frequency of love.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

This week, notice where power struggles show up in your life – in a disagreement with a partner, a moment of frustration with a colleague, or an urge to change something outside yourself to feel better inside. Pause before choosing the horizontal path. Ask yourself: Am I trying to control, or am I trying to grow? What would it look like to change myself here instead of the situation around me? Each time you choose the vertical path, you take one more step toward Authentic Power.

Create the life you desire by choosing love over fear. Learn how HERE

In this Soul Feast, Gary Zukav gets to the heart of one of the most transformative distinctions in spiritual evolution: the difference between living as a victim and living as a creator. Drawing on the framework of Authentic Power – and the deeply personal experience of returning home from the hospital following Linda Francis’s Soul transition –

Gary walks listeners through what it actually feels like in the body and mind to be driven by fear, and what becomes possible the moment you make the Responsible Choice to choose love instead.

Gary introduces Emotional Awareness as the practical tool for recognizing which part of your personality is “at the wheel.” Fear shows up as physical pain in your energy processing centers – aching, contracting, churning – paired with critical, judgmental thoughts. It reaches outward, trying to extract from the world what it believes it cannot find within. Gary is clear: this pursuit of external power is the anatomy of victimhood. Whether it is romantic attraction, addiction, or the need for admiration, all trace back to the same root: the pain of powerlessness and the belief that the center of your meaning lives outside of you.

The path out is not found through willpower or the intellect – it is found through intimacy with your own frightened parts and the courageous choice, made moment by moment, to let love move you instead.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

  • (00:02) — The Choice That Defines Everything: Gary opens with the central tension every Soul faces: a new consciousness is being born and the old world is disintegrating. The question is not whether change is coming – it is which world you will make the Responsible Choice to live in.
  • (01:22) — Emotional Awareness: Your Body Doesn’t Lie: Gary breaks down the somatic practice of distinguishing love from fear – where to place your Total Attention, what physical sensations to look for in your energy centers, and why the thoughts of a frightened personality are always critical and judgmental.
  • (03:30) — The Pain of Powerlessness: At the root of every frightened part of the personality – anger, jealousy, resentment, addiction – is the same unbearable pain: the feeling of being intrinsically defective and fundamentally alone. Gary names it plainly and reminds listeners that everyone in the Earth School carries it.
  • (07:52) — Victim or Creator? The Real Definition: Gary reframes victimhood not as weakness but as a structural condition – one that includes romantic attraction, martyrdom, and every addiction. He contrasts this with the Creator who asks not what they can get through external power, but what they can give from the Soul.
  • (11:44) — How to Challenge Fear (Without Fighting It): Becoming intimate with fear – feeling exactly where it lives, watching what it thinks – is the heroic work. The frightened parts of your personality are not obstacles to your spiritual evolution; they are the avenues.
  • (20:24) — The Night Linda Didn’t Come Home: Gary shares the raw account of returning home from the hospital alone for the first time following Linda’s Soul transition. He didn’t follow a protocol; he simply stayed aware in a state of Ready Presence and found the next morning that something fundamental had shifted.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Think of something you’ve reached for – food, a drink, your phone, someone’s approval – when the discomfort got too loud to sit with. What was the feeling underneath that reaching? Where did you feel it in your body? The next time that sensation arrives, Gary invites you to place your attention in your throat, your chest, your solar plexus. Ask: what is this frightened part of me thinking? You don’t have to fix it – just stay with it long enough to remember that you are the one who gets to choose.

Discover a new way of seeing and experiencing the world. Start your journey to multisensory perception HERE.

In this deeply intimate continuation of his journey, Gary Zukav reveals what happens when the boundaries between physical and non-physical reality begin to dissolve. Through his ongoing Spiritual Partnership with Linda Francis after her Soul’s transition, Gary guides listeners through the paradox of profound presence and profound loss existing simultaneously. He shares the bewildering terrain of speaking with Linda daily while also aching for her physical touch – the five-sensory longing to hear her laugh. This is not a story of “getting over” grief; it is a testament to expanding beyond the personality’s limitations to discover a connection that transcends the Earth School’s physical constraints.

The confusion Gary describes is not weakness – it is the natural friction that occurs when frightened parts of the personality demand the world remain as it was, while loving parts recognize a deeper intimacy emerging. His teacher’s instruction seemed impossible: forget about missing Linda and enjoy life. Yet this paradox held the key to Authentic Power.

The pain of the personality can coexist with the reality of the Soul’s presence, and the intellect – designed only for five-sensory perception – cannot reconcile what the heart already knows.

The solution Gary discovered was a Responsible Choice: to experience greater intimacy with Linda, he had to stop clinging to the old forms of their relationship. By setting the intention to relax into joy, he created space for a multisensory connection to emerge – one where Linda appears in morning light, in clouds, and in moments of presence so powerful they fill every cell of his being. This is the promise of multisensory perception: not the loss of those we love, but an expansion into experiencing them in ways the five senses alone could never access.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

  • (00:02) — The Vast Scope of Human Emotion: Gary explores the full range of emotional experience—from rage and victimhood to gratitude and awe—and why you are far more than any single snapshot of feeling.
  • (04:15) — Choosing Between Love and Fear: How the new consciousness gives you the unprecedented ability to distinguish frightened parts of your personality from loving parts, and to make the Responsible Choice of which to act on.
  • (06:50) — “Linda Is With You”: The first words Gary’s teacher spoke after Linda’s Soul’s transition, and why frightened parts of the personality demand the world remain unchanged while love opens to new possibilities.
  • (11:03) — Forgetting About Missing Her: The paradoxical instruction to “forget about missing Linda and enjoy life”—and how setting this intention opened the door to experiencing her multisensory presence more fully.
  • (14:34) — Seeing Linda in Everything: Gary describes the first time he saw Linda in the morning light through trees, in clouds, and felt her presence so powerfully it filled his entire being.
  • (18:14) — Beyond the Intellect’s Limits: Why the intellect was never designed to understand non-physical reality, and how the new consciousness allows you to become what you are rather than just describe it.

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Think of someone you have navigated a transition with – whether through a Soul’s transition, distance, or the shifting forms of a relationship – and recall a moment when you felt their multisensory presence in an unexpected way. Perhaps in nature, in a sudden knowing, or in a feeling that filled you without explanation.

Pause and ask yourself: What if that presence was real? What if the way you have been taught to understand connection is only a limited form of five-sensory perception? What if there are intimacies available to you now that you could not access before? Gently invite yourself to consider that those you love may be closer than your five senses can perceive, waiting for you to make the Responsible Choice to relax into a new way of experiencing their presence.
